title: Compatibility guardrail matrix and soft rollforward strategy for Terraform modules/providers
creator: Aisha Kaur
description: Goal: Produce a single-pane compatibility guardrail matrix that maps module versions, provider version ranges, and Terraform core versions for Private/VPC deployments, and implement a 'soft rollforward' policy that allows safe minor provider bumps under CI and canary coverage. Deliverable is an automated matrix asset (CSV + rendered dashboard), CI gating rules, and an operational upgrade playbook tested on staging clusters.
background: We maintain multiple Terraform modules for VPC, networking, and cluster bootstrap. Past upgrades of provider versions (aws, hashicorp/aws, random, tls, kubernetes) caused subtle drift in behavior and occasional plan/apply failures. The existing pinbook artifacts are fragmented across PRs and spreadsheets. This ticket consolidates compatibility decisions and defines an operational policy that balances safety and progress.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A machine-readable compatibility matrix (CSV) that lists module, module_version, supported_tf_core, provider, provider_min, provider_max, and test_status columns; 2) CI pipeline that validates candidate provider upgrades against the matrix and runs smoke apply/destroy in sandbox; 3) Canary upgrade runbook and dashboard showing canary success rate and key SLOs; 4) A rollback trigger definition and automated revert PR template.
out_of_scope: Full automation of major provider upgrades (those requiring manual code changes) and migration of non-VPC modules. Those will be handled as separate projects.
plan: Phase 1 (Spike): inventory modules and current pins; Phase 2 (Matrix): build CSV generator from module manifests and lockfiles; Phase 3 (CI/Canary): add pipeline jobs and small canary runbook; Phase 4 (Docs): publish playbook and dashboard; Phase 5 (Rollout): apply soft rollforward policy to non-prod and then prod with timeboxed canaries.
technical_decisions:
- Use a central compatibility CSV stored in infra-config repo under /compat/matrix.csv.
- Provider ranges expressed semver-style: e.g., hashicorp/aws: >=4.50, <5.0 for stable modules.
- Soft rollforward allows minor provider bumps (same major) when: compatibility matrix has a green test_status; CI applies sandbox plan/apply; canary cluster passes smoke SLOs.
- Maintain a provider_lockfile.json for snapshots; do not rely solely on .terraform.lock.hcl in every repo.
- Rollforward automated only when all dependent modules in the same family are green.
implementation_steps: 1) Repo inventory script (scripts/generate_compat_matrix.sh) that scans modules/*/versions.tf and .terraform.lock.hcl; 2) Emit matrix.csv and commit to infra-config; 3) Create CI job (infra-ci/terraform-compat-check) that consumes matrix.csv and runs plan/apply in sandbox; 4) Canary job to apply provider bump to a single canary VPC and run health-checks; 5) Add monitoring dashboard (Observability: infra-upgrades) with canary results and plan/apply latency/errors; 6) Publish runbook in Confluence and link in PR template.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: provider minor change introduces behavioral change not covered by smoke tests. Mitigation: expand smoke tests to include critical path (routing tables, subnet tags, KMS key usage). Risk: matrix drift if not updated. Mitigation: require matrix update PR with provider bump and link to CI run artifacts.
ci_and_testing:
- New job terraform-compat-check runs when a module or provider version is modified.
- Tests: terraform init/plan/apply for a small fixture, infra smoke tests (connectivity, IAM checks, KMS encryption validation), and a destroy step.
- Failure policy: block merge and open an automated issue in repo if any step fails.
canary_plan:
- Canary target: one staging VPC per region.
- Schedule: rolling canaries during low-traffic windows.
- Duration: minimum 24h observation window for perf/latency SLOs and 72h for stability.
- Metrics: plan/apply success, resource drift alerts, service-level probes, and Console ingestion metrics.
rollback_policy:
- Immediate: if canary fails, run automated terraform apply with previous provider lockfile snapshot.
- PR: open revert PR with explicit revert checklist and require on-call approval.
- Postmortem: mandatory for any rollback with customer impact > low.
progress_updates: 2025-02-14: Spike completed — inventory script prototype created and ran against modules/*; found 27 modules with explicit provider pins.
2025-02-20: Initial matrix generated and committed to infra-config branch compat/initial-matrix; shared with PM and Security for review.
2025-02-25: Cross-team review with Platform and Security — agreed on soft rollforward rules and required smoke test set.
2025-03-01: Added CI terraform-compat-check job (WIP) — currently running sandbox apply/destroy on a subset of modules.
2025-03-04: Implemented canary dashboard skeleton and created PR for canary runbook; awaiting design + oncall feedback.
open_questions: How frequently do we want to refresh provider_lockfile snapshots? (daily vs on-change)
Do we enforce provider range upper bounds strictly (< next_major) or allow e.g., >=4.50, <=4.x?
Who signs off on a production rollforward when canaries are green: Infra oncall + Product?

1) Finish CI job to cover all VPC-related modules (target: 2025-03-10).
2) Add expanded smoke tests for KMS and routing (owner: security infra).
3) Finalize runbook and automate revert PR template (owner: Liam).
4) Schedule pilot rollforward for non-prod on 2025-03-18.
